To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spin of an electron in an one-dimensional quantum dot in a semiconductor nanowire may be rotated by a nonadiabatic cyclic transformation, and that this transformation is exact, in the sense that it is independent of the time-dependent parameters of the transformation.
the spin of an electron confined to a quantum dot in a semiconductor nanowire may be rotated by arbitrary angle by an exact nonadiabatic cyclic evolution in parameter space.
the spin of an electron in an one-dimensional moving quantum-dot is rotated by an arbitrary amount on the Bloch-sphere by cyclic evolution of the parameters that define the system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach for quantum computation based on holonomic transformations.
the study of non-adiabatic holonomy in the presence of spin-orbit coupling in a moving quantum dot in an electron nanowire.
exact analytical nonadiabatic solutions for the evolution of spin-orbit coupled quantum dots.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have shown how to perform an arbitrary rotation of the electron spin in a moving quantum dot in the presence of spin-orbit coupling by means of a cyclic evolution in parameter space.
the nonadiabatic geometric phases are not a property of the system, but a property of the process.
the spin-orbit coupling can be used to perform nonadiabatic spin rotations of the electron spin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spin is rotated by an arbitrary amount by a cyclic evolution, and that the phase is the area of the loop in the parameter plane.

the spin of an electron in an one-dimensional quantum dot can be rotated by an arbitrarily large angle by a cyclic evolution in the parameter space spanned by the time-dependent quantum-dot position and the fictitious oscillator amplitude.

the spin of a single electron in a one dimensional moving quantum dot in the presence of a time-dependent spin-orbital coupling may be rotated by any desired angle by appropriate choice of parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adiabatic approximation is not needed to achieve spin rotations, and the nonadiabaticity is actually an asset in achieving holonomic transformations.
the spin-orbit coupling in the presence of a time-dependent electric field is not only a source of spin precession but can also be used to generate nonadiabatic spin rotations.
the adiabatic condition for spin rotation is much weaker than for spin-orbit qubit rotation.
